variables.policy_prompt_for_subgoal: First update remaining_moves exactly once according to the policy prompt for memory. Then return its head verbatim as choice, with point=null. Valid executable choices are the menu letters A through H, not their action descriptions. For example, an updated remaining_moves string of ['A'] requires choice="A", point=null. The same head rule governs transitions from every subgoal: after a completed command, use the head of the updated suffix, including repeating the same option when two consecutive entries match. Do not choose a direction from highlights alone or remove the current head again after choosing it. At episode start, apply the same output rule to the head of the complete list extracted from the demonstration. If visual evidence is ambiguous later, continue to follow the stored list because the controller completes each command before the next decision. For an unexpected state with an empty list or an invalid head, return choice="A", point=null as a deterministic fallback; this is not a claimed continuation of the demonstrated pattern.

fields.name: remaining_moves
fields.description: When memory is empty and demonstration frames are present, read the entire demonstration chronologically and write its complete ordered list of target-to-target menu letters. Serialize remaining_moves as a list string with single-quoted menu letters separated by comma-space, for example ['B', 'F']; serialize the empty list as []. Read the incoming string as its ordered list of letters, apply the update rules below, and write the resulting list in this exact representation at every step. Identify the starting target and each successive reached target using highlight changes together with sustained wrist motion. Treat marker labels such as 'highlighted area' and 'highlighted target' as possible references to lattice targets: identify their lattice cells from their positions, not their label wording. Include the starting target as the source of the first transition, and assign both source and destination to lattice rows and columns before encoding each move. Highlights can retain the previous target, so do not interpret the displayed order of highlighted coordinates as travel order. Each neighboring-target transition is one move, even when consecutive transitions have the same direction. Ignore pauses and small coordinate fluctuations; exclude the reset into execution. Before encoding each direction, identify the source and destination targets' rows and columns in the target lattice. Use sustained wrist motion to establish travel order, not raw wrist displacement signs to classify directions. Targets in the same perspective-slanted column remain in that column despite a small image x displacement: a row change alone is forward or backward. A diagonal requires a change into an adjacent column as well as an adjacent row. Larger y means forward, smaller y backward, larger x left, and smaller x right. Encode forward A, backward B, left C, right D, forward-left E, forward-right F, backward-left G, backward-right H. At every later decision step with carried memory, the oracle has completed the preceding command: remove exactly the first entry of the incoming list and write the resulting suffix. This removal occurs once per decision, not once per observed frame or highlight change. Keep the new first entry in the written list because its command has not yet executed. If the incoming list is empty, retain []. If neither demonstration nor carried memory is available, write []. e.g. ['E', 'D', 'G', 'H']
fields.annotation: An ordered list of menu letters for the demonstrated target-to-target moves not yet completed in execution, including the move to command at this decision step. Serialize the field as a list string with single-quoted menu letters separated by comma-space, for example ['B', 'F']; serialize the empty list as []. Use this exact representation at every step. Extract one move per demonstrated transition between neighboring targets; preserve consecutive identical moves and ignore pauses, image jitter, and the reset from demonstration to execution. At the first decision step store the complete list. At each subsequent decision step remove the one move completed since the preceding decision. Do not remove the move being selected at the current step. Episode 3 values at steps 1–4 are ['E', 'D', 'G', 'H'], ['D', 'G', 'H'], ['G', 'H'], ['H']. Episode 10 values are ['A', 'H', 'H'], ['H', 'H'], ['H']. Episode 34 values are ['A', 'H', 'D', 'F'], ['H', 'D', 'F'], ['D', 'F'], ['F']. Episode 97 values are ['B', 'H', 'A'], ['H', 'A'], ['A']. Episode 99 values are ['D', 'G', 'B', 'D'], ['G', 'B', 'D'], ['B', 'D'], ['D']. e.g. ['E', 'D', 'G', 'H']

If visual evidence is ambiguous later, continue to follow the stored list because the controller completes each command before the next decision. For an unexpected state with an empty list or an invalid head, command A as a deterministic fallback; this is not a claimed continuation of the demonstrated pattern.

history.critique:
field remaining_moves, POLICY PROMPT
  At the first decision for retracing a demonstrated stick pattern, the first demonstrated transition moved backward within one grid column, with only a small increase in image x due to perspective. The policy encoded backward-left and wrote ["G","E"] instead of the annotated ["B","E"]. This is a PREDICTABILITY failure in extracting the list, and it also produces the wrong first subgoal. Strengthen the existing grid-based direction rule: identify source and destination rows and columns from the target lattice before encoding directions. A small x displacement between targets in the same perspective-slanted column is not a column change; a diagonal requires movement into an adjacent column as well as an adjacent row. For example, travel from approximately [113, 85] to [92, 89] stays in the same column and is B, not G. Use sustained wrist motion to establish travel order, not raw wrist displacement signs to classify diagonals. The field remains the ordered list of demonstrated moves not yet completed, including the current command. Initialize it from the complete demonstration when demonstration frames and empty incoming memory are present; for example, ["B","E"]. At each later decision with carried memory, remove exactly its first entry because the preceding oracle command has completed. Do not remove the newly selected command.

the policy prompt for subgoal
  When retracing the pattern after a completed backward-right command, the updated memory correctly contained ["A"], but the policy returned the action description 'move forward' rather than the executable menu label 'A'. The memory was sufficient and correctly updated; the policy prompt's description-based command wording left the output contract unclear, breaking SUFFICIENCY for selecting an executable menu option. Replace the head-to-action-description output rule with: first update remaining_moves once using the policy prompt for memory, then return its head verbatim as choice, with point=null. Valid choices are the letters A through H, not their action descriptions. Thus ["A"] requires choice='A', point=null. Apply this rule at initialization and after every completed command, including consecutive identical letters, without removing the head again after selection. Express the existing empty-list or invalid-head fallback as choice='A', point=null as well; it is only a deterministic fallback, not a demonstrated continuation.

history.critique:
refused
  While initializing memory to retrace a demonstrated stick pattern, the policy correctly chose C for the first move but encoded the final demonstrated transition as H instead of G. That transition ran from [126, 156] to [102, 180]: the destination is in a smaller-y row and a larger-x column, making it backward-left. The annotated complete memory was ["C", "E", "C", "G"], whereas the policy wrote ["C", "E", "C", "H"]. This was a memory-output error, not a missing fact or an unresolved PREDICTABILITY condition: the existing policy prompt for memory explicitly requires identifying source and destination lattice cells, defines smaller y as backward and larger x as left, and maps backward-left to G. The report itself acknowledges that the convention was supplied but misapplied. No annotation change, additional memory field, or subgoal-policy prompt change is warranted; the existing rules already determine the correct value and the correct first subgoal. The proposed trajectory-specific correction is therefore not passed on.

applied.refused: No changes committed. The report proposes no substantive correction: the existing lattice-based direction rule already identifies a smaller-y row and larger-x column transition as backward-left, encoded G. The incorrect H is a misapplication of that explicit rule, not missing memory or an ambiguous transition condition. A trajectory-specific example, additional field, or subgoal-policy prompt change would not resolve a specification gap. The earlier lattice-classification and executable-menu-label corrections remain unchanged.

history.critique:
field remaining_moves, ANNOTATOR PROMPT
  At the initial decision for retracing a demonstrated stick-motion pattern, the policy correctly selected the first movement and recovered the complete movement sequence. However, it wrote double-quoted lists without comma spaces, while the annotated memory used single-quoted entries separated by comma-space. This is a textual PREDICTABILITY mismatch, not a missing movement fact. Specify one canonical representation shared with the policy prompt: a list string with single-quoted menu letters and a space after each comma, for example ['B', 'F']; use [] for the empty list. Replace conflicting examples throughout the rule. The field still holds the ordered demonstrated movements not yet completed, including the movement selected at the current decision. Write the complete list at the first decision and remove exactly one completed movement at each subsequent decision; preserve repeated letters.

field remaining_moves, POLICY PROMPT
  When demonstration frames were present at the initial decision, the policy correctly extracted the demonstrated movement sequence and chose its first command, but serialized the memory with double quotes and no comma spaces rather than the annotation's single quotes and comma-space separators. The policy prompts and annotations therefore permitted different textual answers for the same field, breaking PREDICTABILITY at the representation level. Require remaining_moves to be written as a list string with single-quoted menu letters separated by comma-space, for example ['B', 'F'], and [] when empty; replace all conflicting examples. Retain the existing extraction and update semantics: when demonstration frames are present with no carried memory, extract and write the complete ordered sequence; at a later decision with carried memory, remove exactly its first entry because the preceding oracle command has completed. Write the suffix in the same canonical format, retaining the move being selected now. No additional field or visual inference is needed.

history.critique:
field remaining_moves, POLICY PROMPT
  When retracing a demonstration consisting of one backward move along a perspective-slanted column, the starting marker was labeled 'highlighted area' rather than 'highlighted target'. The destination lay one row above it in the same column, with a small decrease in image x. The policy wrote ['G'] and selected backward-left, whereas the required memory was ['B']. No missing information was reported. This is a PREDICTABILITY failure in demonstration extraction, not a need for additional memory: the existing same-column rule already implies B, but should explicitly cover differently labeled starting markers. Clarify that 'highlighted area' and 'highlighted target' can both identify lattice targets. Assign both source and destination to lattice rows and columns before encoding the transition; never omit the source because its label says area. For example, a source near [102, 154] and destination near [82, 151] belong to the same rightmost image column, so their transition is backward B, not a diagonal. Small perspective-induced x shifts do not change column identity; backward-left G requires a destination in an adjacent larger-x column. Keep the existing field meaning and update timing: remaining_moves holds the ordered uncompleted demonstrated menu letters, including the current command; initialize from all demonstration transitions when demonstration frames are present with empty incoming memory, and remove exactly one leading entry at each later decision after oracle completion. Preserve the exact list-string format, for example ['B']. No additional field or change to annotations is needed.

At every later decision step with carried memory, the oracle has completed the preceding command: remove exactly the first entry of the incoming list and write the resulting suffix. This removal occurs once per decision, not once per observed frame or highlight change. Keep the new first entry in the written list because its command has not yet executed. If the incoming list is empty, retain []. If neither demonstration nor carried memory is available, write []. e.g. ['E', 'D', 'G', 'H']

variables.policy_prompt_for_subgoal: First update remaining_moves exactly once according to the policy prompt for memory. Then return its head verbatim as choice, with point=null. Valid executable choices are the menu letters A through H, not their action descriptions. For example, an updated remaining_moves string of ['A'] requires choice="A", point=null. The same head rule governs transitions from every subgoal: after a completed command, use the head of the updated suffix, including repeating the same option when two consecutive entries match. Do not choose a direction from highlights alone or remove the current head again after choosing it. At episode start, apply the same output rule to the head of the complete list extracted from the demonstration. If visual evidence is ambiguous later, continue to follow the stored list because the controller completes each command before the next decision. For an unexpected state with an empty list or an invalid head, return choice="A", point=null as a deterministic fallback; this is not a claimed continuation of the demonstrated pattern.
